l: A. All department employees shall be subject to disciplinary action for acts of misconduct.
B. In reference to civil service employees, misconduct is defined as any act committed or omitted as required by the twelve (12) rules listed in General Order 410.02(B). TBP 2.04

C. The Professional Standards Division is designated by the Chief of Police as the official repository for all complaints received related to police employees. The Professional Standards Division shall provide periodic reports to the Chief regarding the current status of all investigations and shall keep the Chief apprised of any incident resulting in discipline as defined in General Order 410.02 (A). TBP 2.06
A. The form of disciplinary action for civil service employees may be:
a. In cases involving a felony conviction.

B. The following twelve (12) rules as set forth in Chapter 143, Local Government Code, and the Rules and Regulations of the City of Fort Worth Civil Service Commission, are causes for written coachings, reprimands, and/or disciplinary action, including removal or suspension for civil service employees.
1. Conviction of a felony or other crime involving moral turpitude.

a. Conviction of a felony is cause for termination and conviction of a class A or B misdemeanor may be cause for disciplinary action or indefinite suspension. (Chapter 143, Local Government Code, Section 143.056).
2. Violation of the provisions of the City of Fort Worth charter.
5. Discourtesy to the public or to fellow employee while the officer is in the line of duty.
6. Acts showing lack of good moral character.
7. Drinking intoxicants while on-duty or intoxication while off-duty.
9. Refusal or neglect to pay just debts.
11. Shirking duty or cowardice at fires, if applicable.
12. Violation of any of the rules, regulations, or any orders of the police department.

A. Disciplinary procedures for non-civil service personnel are governed by the City of Fort Worth Personnel Rules and Regulations. Supervisors should refer to the Personnel Rules and Regulations for General Employees and consult with Police Employment Services when taking disciplinary action against a non-sworn employee.
1. Personnel complaint - an allegation, received from any source, of misconduct or violation of policy by a department employee.
2. Personnel complaint form - a form completed by Internal Affairs that is signed by the complaining or reporting party.

3. External complaints - any complaint originating from a person who is not a sworn employee in the Fort Worth Police Department, including, but not limited to, complaints from citizens and complaints from non-sworn City employees.

4.Internal complaints - any complaint originating from a sworn employee of the Fort Worth Police Department, including misconduct observed or reported by a sworn employee of the Fort Worth Police Department.
5. Complaining Party/Complainant - is a person making a complaint that they were harmed by the officer’s alleged misconduct.

6. Reporting Party - is a person who is a witness or third-party source of information regarding alleged misconduct. If the Department initiates a complaint on the basis of reported information, a supervisor or Internal Affairs investigator can be the reporting party for the complaint.

1. All complaints against police employees shall be received, investigated, and disposed of in accordance with the procedures set forth herein in addition to the City Personnel Rules and Regulations, the Meet and Confer Agreement, and Civil Service law, as applicable. TBP 2.06

2. Fort Worth Police Department personnel shall inform any person who wishes to make a complaint against a police officer or police department employee of the existence of the formal complaint procedure and, without unnecessary delay, contact and refer such persons to a police field supervisor, Internal Affairs, or the Police Oversight Monitor. TBP 2.04
3. All personnel complaints shall be accepted and all Personnel Complaint forms shall be completed by Internal Affairs without unnecessary delay whenever: TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
a. The complaint is of misconduct of a nature which, if true, would normally result in a form of disciplinary action outlined in General Order 410.02.
b. The complaint is received from a source outside the department, i.e., citizen complaint, or the alleged violation involves an incident of serious nature.

4. A Personnel Complaint form shall not be completed when complaints are solely about department policies or procedures, as opposed to conduct in violation of a policy or procedure. If a complaint is determined to concern department policies or procedures and no misconduct is indicated, and the incident cannot be explained to the complaining person’s satisfaction, that person shall be referred to the organizational entity having administrative control over the subject matter. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
5. A reporting supervisor shall not have the responsibility of generating a Personnel Complaint Form. Internal Affairs will generate all Personnel Complaint forms. TBP 2.04

6. Personnel Complaint forms shall be witnessed when an allegation of misconduct is received from a source other than sworn personnel. In instances where a valid reason exists for not obtaining the reporting party’s signature, the signature of the Internal Affairs investigator in the “Reporting Party” block will be considered a valid substitute for the signature of the reporting party.

7. A supervisor shall not conduct an investigation of alleged misconduct if they are the complaining party, the ultimate decision-maker regarding disciplinary action, or if they have any personal involvement regarding the alleged misconduct. In such instances, the supervisor will report the event to their immediate supervisor who will either obtain preliminary information regarding the complaint and generate a Blue Team with attached information, or assign another supervisor to do so. (If the employee finds it uncomfortable to report an issue to their immediate supervisor, then they can follow the procedures outlined in G.O. 205.01 (B)(1)). The Blue Team will then be forwarded:
a. Directly to Internal Affairs if the complaint is received from citizen or non-sworn personnel; or
b.Through the chain of command to the Division Commander/Captain if an internal or administrative complaint.
C. When an external complaint, e.g., citizen complaint, is received by Communications/Field Supervision (29CCO):
1. Supervisor call shall be generated and be dispatched to the appropriate field sergeant.

2. The call taker should only obtain the complaining party’s name, phone number, and the officer about whom they are making a complaint. Under no circumstances are Call Takers, Dispatchers, or Dispatch Supervisors to screen or discourage callers who wish to make a complaint against a police officer/employee from doing so.
3. The sergeant/supervisor’s unit number shall be the only information placed in the CAD details rather than the officer’s name.

4. Whenever possible, the call should be dispatched to the officer’s direct supervisor. If the supervisor is unavailable, then it should be dispatched to a sergeant on the same patrol team. As a last resort, it should be dispatched to any supervisor within the same division.

a. Without discouraging the complaining party from making a complaint, the responding supervisor will, to the best of their ability, obtain the nature of the alleged violation, and initiate a Blue Team incident, if warranted.

b. The responding supervisor shall meet in person with the complainant. If the supervisor is unable to meet with the person or will be delayed for a substantial amount of time due to other duties, the supervisor shall contact another supervisor to meet with the person. A supervisor may contact the complainant by phone if the complainant has left the original call location and is several miles beyond the city limits of Fort Worth. Unless exigent circumstances exist, supervisors shall personally meet with complainant. The responding supervisor shall capture the interaction on their body-worn camera or in-car video, and document the interaction and tag the video accordingly.

c. The supervisor shall initiate a “Personnel Complaint -Sworn” incident on Blue Team with the details conveyed to the supervisor by the complaining party and shall forward the Blue Team to Internal Affairs within 24 hours.
(1) If the complaint merely poses questions on department practice and policy:
(a) The supervisor will document the result of the investigation in the call disposition.
(b) The body-worn camera and/or in-car video will be uploaded to Evidence.com.

d. When a personnel complaint is received from a third-party source, the information should be documented by the field supervisor, attached to a Blue Team, and forwarded directly to Internal Affairs. The third-party source shall be asked to sign the Personnel Complaint form, generated by Internal Affairs as the reporting party. Unless the personnel complaint is validated by subsequent interview of an actual party to the incident, the final disposition of such complaint shall not be listed on an officer’s Internal Affairs record. All reports related to such complaints shall be filed as miscellaneous memorandums by Internal Affairs.

e. When a personnel complaint is received from an intoxicated person, the information should be documented by the field supervisor, attached to a Blue Team, and forwarded directly to Internal Affairs. The complaining person shall be re-interviewed by Internal Affairs at the earliest opportunity after having regained sobriety. During the re-interview, the complaining person shall be asked to sign the Personnel Complaint form, generated by Internal Affairs. Unless the personnel complaint is validated by subsequent interview of the intoxicated person, the final disposition of such complaint shall not be listed on an officer’s Internal Affairs record. All reports related to such complaints shall be filed as miscellaneous memorandums by Internal Affairs.

a. When any supervisor becomes aware of possible misconduct, either through personal observation or other means, except for complaints received from external sources as described in the previous section, the supervisor shall take action to prevent continuation or aggravation of the incident. The supervisor shall also conduct a preliminary investigation, which shall include, when applicable:
(1) Names, identification numbers, and assignments of all involved employees, including employees who are witnesses.

(2) Names, addresses and telephone numbers of the complaining person and any known witnesses to the incident who are not department employees. Times, locations, and business and residential telephone numbers where these individuals may be contacted shall be indicated.
(3) A statement from the complaining person obtained by an interview of that person by the reporting supervisor.
(4) Photographs of actual or claimed injuries to the complaining person.
(5) Photographs shall be taken in all cases involving allegations of excessive force.
(6) Any available information regarding medical treatment obtained by the complaining person as a result of the incident.
(7) The disposition of any evidence obtained.

b. Minor policy violations or Coaching issues that will not reflect discredit upon the department, but which indicate a need for some form of corrective action and/or training, may be dealt with by the involved officer’s immediate supervisor with the review and concurrence of the involved employee’s division commander/captain. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06

(1) Coaching Issues are minor, internal department issues requiring supervisory coaching above the level of verbal coaching, but not arising to the level of a Written Reprimand. These are clear-cut issues not requiring a personnel complaint or an Internal Affairs investigation. Examples would include reoccurrences of not activating camera, late for roll call, etc. The determination of the handling of these issues at the unit level would be at the discretion of the Commander/Captain of the Division.

(2) With Division Commander/Captain approval documented on Blue Team, the supervisor of appropriate rank may issue a Supervisor’s Coaching or Captain’s Coaching form, generate and attach the form to the appropriate Blue Team, and forward the Blue Team directly to the Internal Affairs. This will NOT apply to citizen or non-sworn initiated complaints.
(a) A copy of the completed coaching form will be attached or documented on the Blue Team and forwarded to Internal Affairs within two (2) weeks.

(3) If the Commander/Captain determines that the investigation could result in discipline as defined under General Order 410.02 A (i.e., suspension, demotion, indefinite suspension, or termination), the Division Commander/Captain shall forward the investigation to Internal Affairs within four (4) days of receipt of the Blue Team.

3. Division commanders/captains have the primary responsibility for investigating personnel complaints made against employees of their divisions. A division commander/captain who becomes aware of any allegation of misconduct shall monitor all resulting activities and shall ensure that personnel under their command have fulfilled their responsibilities provided in this order. A division commander/captain may request that Internal Affairs conduct an investigation on any allegation of misconduct or personnel complaint. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06

1. A Personnel Complaint form shall not be completed for personnel complaints received from anonymous sources; however, when information is received by a supervisor which originated from an anonymous source, the supervisor shall complete a Blue Team detailing the information received and forward it to Internal Affairs. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
2. If the information received is of a nature that would jeopardize the integrity of an investigation by being reduced to writing, it shall be handled in accordance with General Order 410.05.

3. If the information received describes misconduct of a nature which, if true, would normally result in a form of disciplinary action outlined in General Order 410.02, a preliminary investigation will be conducted by Internal Affairs.

4. When warranted, the allegation of misconduct shall be reported on a Personnel Complaint form. If the identity of the anonymous reporting party cannot be determined or the reporting party, if identified, refuses to sign the Personnel Complaint form, the signature of the Internal Affairs investigator in the “Reporting Party” block will be considered a valid substitute for the signature of the reporting party. TBP 2.04

F. When an employee other than a supervisor is made aware of a complaint either through personal observation or other means, of possible misconduct they shall, if applicable, take corrective action to preclude continuation or escalation of the incident and shall immediately notify a supervisor. TBP 2.04

A. When a personnel complaint or incident is of a nature that the integrity of the investigation may be compromised or jeopardized by reducing the incident to writing, the reporting supervisor shall immediately report the incident to their lieutenant, who shall report said incident to the lieutenant of Internal Affairs.

B. If the reporting supervisor has reason to believe the integrity of the investigation may be compromised by passage through normal channels, the supervisor shall personally report the incident directly to the lieutenant of Internal Affairs. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06

C. When immediate action is required or the seriousness of the incident is such that it may subject the department to severe criticism or liability, the reporting supervisor shall provide immediate notification to the involved employee’s division commander/captain and to the Captain of the Professional Standards Division. If after hours, this notification shall be made through a callback notification through the Communications Division. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06

1. In incidents of this magnitude, the Chief of Police or the appropriate Bureau Assistant Chief may place the involved employee on Restricted or Detached duty, with pay, and shall, when applicable, take custody of the employee’s badge, identification card, and service weapon (unless personally owned).

2. If the decision is made to place an officer on restricted or detached duty, Internal Affairs shall be contacted to facilitate the process, complete required documentation, and take custody of the involved employees’ badge, commission card, and service weapon (unless personally owned).
3. The reinstatement of the officer and return of equipment can only be authorized by the affected officer’s bureau Assistant Chief.

A. The lieutenant or above of Internal Affairs shall act in a staff advisory capacity when necessary. The Internal Affairs Lieutenant may assume responsibility for the investigation of any personnel complaint when, in the opinion of the lieutenant, it is advisable to do so. The lieutenant also has the authority to obtain the advice and assistance of any departmental entity.
B. Internal Affairs shall assume responsibility for an internal or external personnel complaint designated as a Tier One Investigation. An investigation is classified as Tier One when:
1. It has been alleged an employee has committed any felony or Class A or B misdemeanor.
2. The allegation of misconduct is against employees of more than one division.
3. The investigation involves an allegation of:
(b) Sexual harassment or inappropriate conduct of a sexual nature,
(d) Disparate treatment or inappropriate comment due to gender, race, ethnicity, age, or sexual orientation,
(e) Retaliation for reporting the misconduct of another, or
4. The allegations have attracted media attention.
5. The Internal Affairs Lieutenant determines it is in the Department’s best interest.
C. Tier Two Investigations will consist of cases not falling under the above criteria. Internal Affairs will assume responsibility for all Tier Two Investigations which involve one of the following:
1. Any complaint received from citizen or non-sworn personnel not meeting Tier One criteria.

2. Internal complaint designated for investigation following consultation with a Captain or Commander over a division that will likely result in discipline as defined under General Order 410.02 A (i.e., suspension, demotion, indefinite suspension, or termination).
3. Cases as determined by the Internal Affairs Lieutenant or the Internal Affairs Administrative Sergeant

D. The Internal Affairs investigator or supervisor performing the investigation shall provide the employee with the written allegations in the complaint no less than 48 hours before the initial interview or requesting any inter-office correspondence or other correspondence related to the incident from the employee. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
NOTE: The 48-hour notice does not apply to on-scene investigations that occur immediately after an incident.

A. If an employee of the department is detained or arrested for any criminal offense within the City of Fort Worth, the officer detaining or arresting the employee shall immediately notify a supervisor of the division in which the employee is detained or arrested.

B. A supervisor who has been notified that an employee of the department has been arrested or detained shall immediately proceed to the scene and shall ensure that a lieutenant or above of the patrol division in which the incident occurs is immediately notified.
C. The lieutenant of the patrol division shall ensure immediate notification is made to:
3. The commander/captain of the employee’s division of assignment.

D. Internal Affairs shall conduct an investigation whenever an employee is arrested for or believed to be a principal suspect in a felony or class A or B misdemeanor offense. When warranted, Special Investigations personnel shall be responsible for submitting the criminal case to the District Attorney for consideration of criminal prosecution. The Captain of the Professional Standards Division has the discretion to assume responsibility for investigations related to class C misdemeanor violations.

E. When any employee of the department is detained or becomes aware that they are believed to be the principal suspect in a criminal offense, other than minor traffic violations committed outside the City of Fort Worth, including offenses committed outside of the State of Texas, the employee shall as soon as possible notify a supervisor.

1. All employees of the department must notify a supervisor as soon as possible regarding any changes, corrections, or updates to criminal charges, including criminal convictions for offenses other than minor traffic violations, within the employee’s criminal history report.

F. When any employee of the department becomes aware that another employee has been detained or is believed to be a principal actor in a criminal offense, other than minor traffic violations committed outside the city, the employee shall immediately notify a supervisor.

G. Any supervisor who is notified regarding the detainment or arrest of an employee by another law enforcement agency, other than minor traffic violations, shall ensure that immediate notification is made to Internal Affairs and to the division commander of the involved employee.
H. Internal Affairs personnel shall respond to the scene or to the indicated outside agency when the incident involves an alleged felony or class A or B misdemeanor.
1. A supervisor from the involved employee’s division of assignment shall respond on alleged class C misdemeanor violations if the violation is of a magnitude to require immediate investigation.
a. Regardless of whether a supervisor responds to the scene, a Personnel Complaint form shall still be prepared and processed.
2. The responding supervisor shall conduct a preliminary investigation and a Personnel Complaint form shall be prepared and processed as described in General Order 410.06.

3. The responding supervisor shall advise concerned members of the outside agency that the preliminary investigation is for internal administrative purposes only and that any evidence obtained by the responding supervisor solely as a result of interviewing the involved employee shall not be disclosed to the agency conducting the criminal investigation. Responding supervisors shall exercise extreme care not to interfere with the investigation of the outside agency.
A. Administrative investigations which may result in disciplinary action shall be completed within thirty (30) calendar days from the date the complaint is received or initiated. TBP 2.05
Note: Due to the complicated nature of some investigations, the investigation deadline may be extended by the Operational Command Deputy Chief.

B. Unless approved by the Chief of Police or designee, the complete administrative investigation review, employee notification, and issuance of any discipline will be the responsibility of the chain of command of the officer at the time of the incident or misconduct. If an employee is moved prior to the completion of the investigation, the chain-of-command responsible for that employee at the time the incident occurred will continue the investigation, review and notifications. Reassignment of the officer does not reassign responsibility of any part of the investigative, notification or discipline process.

C. The review by the chain of command shall be completed within twenty-one (21) calendar days of the date the investigation is completed or the date the investigative report is received from Internal Affairs. The chain of command may receive an extension with approval from the Chief of Police. TBP 2.05

D. Internal Affairs shall submit the completed investigation to the involved employee’s Commander/Captain. The Commander/Captain will designate a Lieutenant to review the case (depending on the rank of the involved employee this can differ). Example: involved employee is a Lieutenant, the case will be sent to the Deputy Chief, who will designate a Commander/Captain to review the case). This person shall:

1. Prepare a summary report using the “Field Write-up” template provided on the internal police department portal. This report will have findings for each allegation and, if necessary, make a recommendation for discipline. Each allegation will be resolved with one of the following dispositions:
a. Unfounded: The investigation reveals sufficient evidence to believe the complained of act did not occur.
b. Exonerated: The investigation reveals the complained of act occurred but was legal, proper, and justified.
c. Not-Sustained: The investigation discloses insufficient evidence to believe the complained of act either did or did not occur.
d. Sustained: The investigation discloses sufficient evidence to conclude the complained of act occurred.
2. Discuss the findings with the involved officer’s sergeant (or applicable rank depending on the rank of the involved employee) to determine an appropriate discipline recommendation,
3. Discuss the findings and recommendation for disciplinary action with the involved employee in person, documenting the meeting in the summary report, and
4. Forward the completed investigation and summary report for review to the next level in the chain of command.

E. When a completed investigation is forwarded for review, the next higher level will meet with the preceding level to discuss the disciplinary recommendations. Each ascending level shall document the results of that meeting as follows:
1. If the next level up concurs with the lower-level findings, they will document concurrence in the comments section of the Blue Team report. No additional IOC is necessary.

2. If the next level up disagrees with the lower-level finding, the higher level will generate and attach a new IOC to document their explanation for disagreement, their findings, and their recommendations.
3. Once they complete their findings, each level of the chain that provides a recommendation for discipline should meet with the officer to give their recommendation.

F. The review process will continue moving through ascending levels in the chain of command until it reaches one level above the designated permissible discipline levels established by the Meet & Confer contract in effect at the time the misconduct occurred. Example: If the conduct occurred during 2018, and the recommended discipline is a three (3)- day suspension or less, then a commander would issue the discipline and notate in the BlueTeam comments which deputy chief concurred with the discipline.

G. Disciplinary suspensions may only be served by the rank of commander and above. Captains and below are not permitted to issue a disciplinary suspension. Meetings between the appointed rank and the officer for all disciplinary suspensions shall be scheduled by the appointed rank and held in the office of Internal Affairs or an agreed upon location. Internal Affairs personnel will assist the appointed rank by generating the appropriate paperwork for the meeting.
H. Upon completion of the review and issuance of discipline, the final reviewer shall forward the investigation and all related documents to Internal Affairs.
I. Under no circumstances shall any level of review change or require a change in conclusions and/or recommendations of another.

J. If any level of review determines that additional investigation is required, the further investigation shall normally be conducted by the supervisor or Internal Affairs investigator conducting the original investigation.

K. When an investigation subsequently discloses additional allegations of misconduct which were not described in the original personnel complaint, and the classification of the original complaint is other than sustained, a new complaint form shall be prepared and a supplemental investigative report completed. When any allegation of misconduct in the original personnel complaint is sustained, the new allegations may be recorded as separate supplemental charges in the investigative report for the original complaint.
